wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: An unpublished Pentagon estimate put the Iran war above $47 billion as Trump said the US may strike Iran as soon as Sunday, and Israel's army chief reportedly warned Washington off. In Tehran, Khamenei backed the conditions for peace talks, while Iran threatened Sinokor's tankers with legal action for breaking its Hormuz transit rules.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The Iran war and the Hormuz closure cut Gulf supply, and OPEC+ held output targets its Gulf members already miss. Saudi Arabia intercepted 10 ballistic missiles as the Houthis claimed a strike on its pipeline. The cost landed on importers: the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars to defend the rupee, and Iraq ran short of fuel.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The Hormuz disruption set the price: traffic through the strait ran 11% below normal as of 18 October under an IRGC blockade, and the Houthis said they targeted Saudi oil sites. Ukrainian drones hit oil facilities in St Petersburg. Rubio answered by pressing India's Reliance to refine more Venezuelan crude.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news came from the Gulf: Qatar, its own exports squeezed by Hormuz, agreed to import up to 4 million tons of US gas a year, and Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days. None of it accounts for the swings in the US price itself.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Governments moved against dearer bread: Egypt offered mills wheat from LE16,500 a tonne, and Pakistan raised its support price to Rs4,500 a maund. Germany urged Russia to halt Black Sea attacks threatening grain supplies. All of it came after the last monthly reading, so none of it explains the rise.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: Recent food reporting was about who can afford to eat rather than about the grain market: 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry in September, Afghan acute hunger reached a record 15.9 million, and Nigeria's food inflation rose to 19.59%. None of it explains the price of rice.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: The latest reading predates this month's supply news, so none of it explains the climb: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine for over a week, Mysteel sees China's fourth-quarter refined copper output falling, and Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Nothing here names the cause of the climb, only its cost: Bank of America is carrying $109 billion of unrealized bond losses, the mechanism that sank Silicon Valley Bank in 2023. Long-term French yields rose in step from 4% in August, and the Fed is expected to hold rates, with TD Securities forecasting 3 dissents.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion, and Goldman expects $1.7 trillion in 2027 share unlocks to be matched by buybacks, but neither story accounts for the index's path over the window.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The index's heaviest members spent the fortnight paying for AI: Meta raised $95bn in new stock for data centres, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyeing part of it, and Microsoft forecast $175 billion of capital spending while offering 60,000 buyouts. Meta was also told to pay $25bn in New Mexico. None of these stories accounts for the index's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The US spent the fortnight trying to cut fuel costs before the midterm elections: Trump's deal with Putin sent a first 40,000-tonne cargo of Russian diesel toward New York, due after the vote, and the US weighed lifting sanctions on Iran's 'shadow fleet'. Diesel is not gasoline, and nothing reported explains the pump price itself.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar, whose cargoes normally leave through Hormuz, is sending a tanker across the Red Sea toward Poland and has agreed to buy US gas itself. Liquefied natural gas now costs triple its pre-crisis price, and in the UK gas accounts for £161 of a £180 rise in household bills.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's news ran to France's school protests becoming a political crisis, a crude oil and diesel crisis, and the ECB saying banks tightened credit conditions; none of it is tied in the input to the price of options on US stocks.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's news from Islamabad was about domestic prices rather than the currency: Rs114 of every Rs379.25 litre of petrol is now tax, Jamaat-i-Islami threatened a march on the capital over that levy, and the 200-unit electricity cliff is being scrapped. None of it explains the rupee's path.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight in Nigeria was dominated by Ebola, which reached the country with 1 confirmed case in Lagos and a patient evacuated to Switzerland, and by Tinubu's re-election launch as food inflation rose to 19.59%. JPMorgan also cleared the first step to a banking licence. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight in Cairo was dominated by the war next door: Egypt's defence council and then its parliament authorised military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthi, and Iran offered to reopen Hormuz shipping. None of that reporting addresses the central bank or the currency, so none of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey sat at the centre of the Iran-war diplomacy: Istanbul hosted mediators, and Ankara submitted the Makkah pact binding it to defend Riyadh. A floating platform set to double Sakarya gas output launched, and the state seized an opposition TV channel. None of it accounts for the lira's slide.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's news from Bangladesh was a measles outbreak that has killed 1,147 people since March, two executions in Saudi Arabia carried out without notice to Dhaka, and the Bede river nomads pushed ashore by a fixed-address system. None of it accounts for the taka's move.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah's slide followed MSCI's move to remove Indonesia from its global indexes, which obliges funds tracking them to sell Indonesian shares and take their dollars home. Jakarta stocks fell to a six-year low, then lost 11.6% in one Friday, the worst day since 1998, before the government announced measures to improve market transparency.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Lebanon dwelt on how years of war have deepened its cost of living crisis, and on Iran's calls for an all-front ceasefire and for Lebanon's sovereignty. None of it accounts for the pound's small drift against the dollar.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Three Jiangsu universities moved November salaries onto the digital yuan, and Hong Kong pitched yuan settlement to Southeast Asia's regional bloc, but neither touches the exchange rate, and nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the yuan's firming.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: Traders say the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars on Wednesday to hold the currency up. India imports most of its oil, and Brent prices kept high by the Iran war and the Hormuz disruption swell the import bill, and with it the demand for dollars that the central bank meets from its reserves.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to win by 4.4 million votes, beating the market's pick, and real futures fell 10% on fears over his fiscal plans. Brazilian companies had moved cash into dollar stablecoins on election day, and Flávio Bolsonaro refused to concede, then left Brazil for the US.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's Mexican news was mostly domestic. Inflation of 3.62% in early October ran above forecasts, AT&T sold its Mexican unit and 24.7 million subscribers to Televisa for $2 billion, and Pemex spills alarmed fishers. None of it accounts for the peso's slide against the dollar.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Pressure came from Paris: protests over France's schools became a political crisis for Macron, with over 1,800 arrested, and the 10-year bond yield hit 4.96%, the highest since 2002. Lagarde pointed to the bond selloff as the European Central Bank headed for a December hike, and EU leaders rejected the seven-year budget.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Doubts about the AI boom sent money into the yen as a haven, lifting it to 156.28 per dollar, a one-month high. Tokyo is weighing wage-driven inflation with the Bank of Japan's rate at 1.25%, a 31-year high, while record foreign flows into US equities kept demand for the dollar strong.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Washington eased the pressure on Russia's export earnings: Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law, and 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel left Primorsk for New York under a deal Lavrov called purely business. Russia kept its key rate at 14%, which keeps ruble savings paying well.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight's South African news was domestic: a budget that cuts the fuel levy until January 2027, a Pretoria judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, and Merz urging Trump to invite South Africa to the G-20 Summit in Miami. None of it accounts for the rand's slide.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: MSCI moved to write rules that would eject bitcoin treasury firms from its indices, and JPMorgan estimated $2.8 billion in outflows from Strategy stock as a result. Google's Willow chip then sharpened the quantum threat to the 6.4 million bitcoin whose public keys are already exposed, and Coinbase urged the network to migrate to quantum-resistant keys now.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The US Senate fell short of the 60 votes the Clarity Act needed, leaving American crypto rules unwritten a week after Patrick Witt became the 3rd White House crypto adviser to go. The trough came as the Fed meeting began and traders de-risked, pulling Bitcoin under $80,000, even as Bitmine kept buying ETH.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Oil near $100 fed an energy-led inflation that pushed the expected rate path higher for longer, and gold, which pays nothing to hold, lost 3.6% in a week, its worst since June. Buying underneath held up: China's central bank added 23 tonnes in September, and gold ETF inflows jumped 71% that month.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The fortnight's AI news was about money: Anthropic filed to list after losing $80.7 billion on $16.3 billion of revenue, Meta raised $95bn of equity for data centres, and Microsoft offered 60,000 buyouts while forecasting $175 billion of capital spending. None of it dates to the mid-month peak.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Putin announced the release of American prisoner Stephen Hubbard during Steve Witkoff's visit to St Petersburg, and the Kremlin confirmed talks in Abu Dhabi, saying Putin wants a final settlement, not a truce. Then 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel sailed from Primorsk for New York. All of it came weeks after the early-October peak.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said mines hit seven tankers in one night and two more supertankers soon after, as four foreign ministers demanded the strait reopen. CENTCOM answered that it had escorted 1.5 billion barrels of Gulf crude, and Tehran now threatens Sinokor's tankers with legal action from 1 November.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran is writing its own transit rules for the strait and threatens Sinokor's tankers with legal action from 1 November. Beyond the strait, Iraq, a major oil producer, is short of fuel; the Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the route around Hormuz; and Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: October's fighting has been on land and in the air rather than at sea: the Houthis fired missiles at Aden, at Riyadh and at the Saudi East-West pipeline, the route that carries crude to Yanbu on the Red Sea. Meanwhile a Qatari gas tanker crossed the Red Sea toward Poland, and China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: With Hormuz shut under a US blockade, Qatar sent an LNG tanker up the Red Sea toward Poland, a cargo that must transit Suez to reach Europe. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia kept the southern approach contested; Egypt's parliament voted to defend the kingdom, and China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The Revolutionary Guards say mines in Hormuz set tankers ablaze, upstream of the crude that crosses this strait to Asian refiners. Vitol says shipping US crude to Asia costs $40 a barrel, and Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027. None of it has yet thinned traffic through Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's reporting on China ran to a spaceplane, AI hardware driving exports, a tech-stock repricing and Kim Jong Un's visit to a Chinese border city. None of it touches shipping through the Taiwan Strait or accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the western Black Sea entered a NATO country's territorial waters for the first time, off Romania, and later sank the Khoryv near Constanța. At least 23 sailors are missing or dead. Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships, and NATO sent patrol planes and drones to guard the grain route.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The news touching this route was about Russian oil. Washington weighed easing sanctions on shadow fleet tankers, and Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began. None of it accounts for the ships passing Gibraltar, and no weather or closure in the input does either.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The month's tanker story was in Hormuz, where the Revolutionary Guards said mines set supertankers ablaze, and Vitol put the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel. None of it has yet shown up as a shift in traffic around the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's news from the sea was elsewhere: a drone sank the cargo ship Khoryv off Constanța, killing one sailor, while the Kremlin confirmed talks with the US and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. Nothing in it accounts for traffic through the strait itself.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The slide ran alongside the Iran war next door: Türkiye warned a fresh assault on Iran risked a wider regional war, Istanbul hosted ministers demanding Hormuz reopen, and Ankara moved to bind itself to Riyadh's defence in the Makkah pact. The government also took over an independent TV news channel. None of it is reported as the cause.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's fortnight brought a 2027 Budget that continued fiscal consolidation, a ban on Waze for civil servants, a Tanaka plant to recover gold from chip scrap, and weddings shrinking across Southeast Asia under inflation. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: MSCI moved to cut Indonesia's status and remove it from its global indexes after months of warnings, which pushes funds that track those indexes to sell. Stocks plunged 10% to a six-year low, then fell 11.6% on Friday, the worst day since 1998.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Doubts about AI spending pushed money into the yen, which reached a one-month high at 156.28 per dollar, and a stronger yen shrinks what Japan's exporters earn abroad. At home the Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate is already a 31-year high, and Tokyo is weighing whether wages, not imports, now drive inflation.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Hong Kong's market news in the fortnight was about how the market works, not what it is worth. A regulator froze HK$4.38 billion over suspected faked public-offering demand, Noetix filed to list, and Valcambi agreed to refine gold in the city. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: China's AI and tech names were repriced: Contemporary Amperex fell 15% despite a 21.2 billion yuan quarterly profit, and robot shares valued at 22 billion yuan drew no bids at 12 billion. Blue chips fell 11 weeks straight, a record, even as September exports surged 36% and growth beat estimates.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: An AI chip rout sent the Kospi down more than 7%, and the doubts spread: Elice closed 30% below its offer price, and SK hynix cancelled a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion. The rebound came when South Korea's economy grew 1% last quarter, three times the forecast, on demand for AI memory chips.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Oil kept high by the Iran war and the Hormuz disruption swelled India's import bill and drained the rupee, and traders say the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars to hold it at 95.02. Money still found new listings: Jio Platforms' offering, India's largest, drew record bids and its shares rose 21.4% on debut.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Indonesia, Singapore's largest gas supplier, cut pipeline exports to keep more for itself, in a city that generates up to 95% of its electricity from gas, and Singapore's foreign minister went to Jakarta. Shipping US crude to Asia reached $40 a barrel as the Hormuz shortage bit. Nothing reported ties either to the index's slide.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: TSMC, roughly a third of the index, posted record profit for the sixth straight quarter in mid-October, and its stock still fell. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the index's run, including a Micron union strike in Taoyuan over bonuses and the power cuts Typhoon Champi brought to Taiwan.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's news this fortnight was domestic: a budget that cuts the fuel levy until January 2027, a judge voiding R12.6 billion in antiretroviral drug awards, and 300 steel jobs at a new Coega mill. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Markets had priced a win for Flávio Bolsonaro. Lula overturned a first-round deficit with 4.4 million votes to spare, and real futures fell 10% on fears for his fiscal plans in what traders called Brazil's Black Monday. Inflation had already broken the target ceiling at 4.62%, and companies moved cash into dollar stablecoins before the result.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Inflation in Mexico hit 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, and AT&T agreed to sell its 24.7 million Mexican subscribers for $2 billion. Neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The week's Argentine news came after the last reading: a court dropped its probe of Milei's $LIBRA endorsement, and First Quantum sought state-backed tax breaks for its $5.25 billion Taca Taca copper mine. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada's main news in the second half of October was Alberta voting 76% to stay in Canada, inflation reaching 3.1% as gasoline rose 27.8% in a year, and Trump cutting 50% tariffs on a few Canadian products such as crates and seaweed. None of it is tied to the index's moves.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Foreign money flowed into US equities at a record pace on the AI boom: Microsoft forecast $175 billion in capital spending, Meta raised $95bn in equity for its data centres, and Anthropic filed to list. China's blue-chip index fell 11 weeks straight over the same stretch, and the Fed is expected to hold rates on Wednesday.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The news from London's biggest lenders was about returns: HSBC's pretax profit hit $9.6 billion in the July-September quarter, and Barclays is paying shareholders £500 million while cutting 5,000 jobs. Neither result accounts for the index's direction.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Ifo business expectations rose for a sixth month, to 91.6, while an ECB survey found credit tightening for euro zone firms and Volkswagen planned to freeze pay for 660,000 workers until 2030. Nothing reported in the period ties any of it to the index's swings.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The slide tracked French borrowing costs: long-term yields rose from 4% in August to above 5%, the 10-year hit its highest since 2002, and the state now borrows above companies. Lagarde has the European Central Bank heading for a December hike, while protests that drew 410,000 across France became a political crisis for Macron.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The mid-October rise ran on ASML, which reported that China's share of its sales had jumped from 14% to 23%, with equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push for export curbs. Since then, customers have been asking ASML for lithography tools for 2029 and 2030, as demand for the machines behind advanced AI chips outruns supply.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's news this fortnight was floods in the east, where Pego took 632 mm of rain in 36 hours; Milei rallying for the far right against Sanchez; and 25,000 marching in Madrid for pensions that keep pace with inflation. None of it reaches the banks that weigh most on the index, and none of it accounts for the slide.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The trough came as the ECB's Panetta warned that rising bond yields would restrain the economy, a pressure that reaches a bank-heavy Italian index first. The ECB then cleared Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy's biggest bank, to bid €32 billion for Monte dei Paschi, the lender the state rescued in 2017.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss news was about Proton's AI interviews of its staff, hijacked Tor exit nodes and an Ebola patient evacuated from Nigeria to Switzerland. None of it reaches the drug and food giants that move the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The fortnight's Swedish financial news was Sweden's central bank reviving its debate over an e-krona as stablecoins and a digital euro loom. That is a question about payments, and nothing reported in the window explains the index's slide or its rebound.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The run-up to Tuesday's election brought polls putting Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu, and reports that Israel's army chief warned Washington off striking Iran. Israel also locked down Hebron after a checkpoint gunfight. None of the reporting ties any of it to the index.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump threatened a US strike on Iran as soon as Sunday, and Tehran answered by naming data centres, cables and AI sites in 7 Gulf states as targets. Prosecutors revived a closed 2016 leak case to charge Comey a third time, and in Detroit Trump attacked Senate candidate El-Sayed.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: September's 3.7% annual inflation, lifted by gasoline, pushed traders toward betting on a hike rather than a cut. Fed Chair Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance in Bangkok, and TD Securities expects 3 dissents against Wednesday's hold.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The bank is heading for a December hike: Lagarde credited a bond selloff, with French debt under pressure, as part of the case. Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%. Credit is already tightening, with loan obstacles hitting 7% of euro zone firms.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: The fortnight's headlines on precious metals were about gold, which eased on a firmer dollar ahead of the Fed decision as conflicting Iran signals clouded the path for rates; none of them addresses silver itself.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove September's reading: prices rose 0.6% in that month alone, more than expected. The figure landed weeks before the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell the next day on fears of tighter policy.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The IMF cut its 2026 Gulf growth forecasts over the prolonged Hormuz closure. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says 7 tankers were hit in one night and a 2-million-barrel supertanker burned after a mine; CENTCOM says its escorts moved 1.5 billion barrels of Gulf crude. Tehran now threatens Sinokor with legal action from 1 November for breaking its transit rules.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The news around the strait was the Houthi war on Saudi Arabia: a drone strike at Shaybah, an attack on Dammam airport, missiles at Aden. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, and a Qatari gas tanker crossed it toward Poland. None of it concerns container ships, and none accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The reporting from the fortnight after this series ends followed Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Saudi oil sites, Riyadh's airport and Aden, and the Makkah pact talks in Tehran. None of it concerns ships bound for Suez, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news centred on other waterways: Iran's threats over Hormuz transits, NATO planes and drones sent to the Black Sea after attacks on shipping, and concern over the Red Sea. The UN also called for action on an 'off the charts' El Niño. None of it concerns traffic through Panama.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's news from these waters was about Hormuz, not Malacca: Iran's mines and transit rules there, and Saudi Arabia arranging to store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027. None of it accounts for traffic through this strait.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: The Houthis carried the war into Saudi Arabia: a drone strike on Shaybah sent Brent to $110.63, an attack at Dammam airport killed two, and Riyadh's airport was declared a military target. The UK sent Typhoons, Egypt's parliament authorised defending Saudi Arabia, and Saudi Arabia's defence minister went to Tehran for talks.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Kyiv accused SpaceX of throttling Starlink terminals, with drones cutting out at 130 km/h, and said the US withheld warning of 16 ballistic missiles before restoring strike intelligence. Trump put new Russia sanctions on hold and pressed Kyiv to make a deal; Witkoff met Putin, and talks moved to Oslo and then Abu Dhabi.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Mojtaba Khamenei endorsed the conditions for peace talks set out by Mohsen Rezaei, Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, and Israel's army chief reportedly warned Washington off striking Iran. Even the Hormuz dispute moved to paper: Iran threatened Sinokor with legal action, not force.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia's grip on China's AI chip market loosened: Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months, taking sales in a market where Nvidia's share had already fallen. Separately, a leaked White House list showed Nvidia gave $25 million toward the ballroom, as Apple did.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: The climb into late October came as iPhone Duo pre-orders opened and were soon backordered into 2027, the same week Apple Intelligence entered China running on Alibaba's Qwen models. Reports of screen problems followed, and Apple said it would replace affected iPhone Duo units, a day before it launched M6 Macs.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google's own news cut both ways: its only UK cloud region failed at 06:08 GMT, it softened its Gmail ad-targeting promise on 16 October, and it halved the price of Gemini 4 Argon to $2 per million input tokens. None of them was reported as the reason the shares fell.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: The fortnight's one story about Amazon's own business was a product launch: AI devices that listen to and keep track of conversations, picked up by 73 outlets. Nothing in it accounts for the share price, and the high and low both fell before that news.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: In mid-October it reported a record profit for the sixth straight quarter, and the shares fell after the results anyway. Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains why investors sold a record quarter.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: The company's own news this fortnight was about cost. It offered buyouts to 60,000 employees while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, and it dropped the Nscale site at Loughton, where grid power for the AI data centre may wait a decade. None of it accounts for the climb in the share.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: The one story about Broadcom in this period was not about its chips: it was among the issuers, alongside Verizon, that objected to the SEC's framework for trading tokenized versions of their shares. Nothing in it accounts for the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX's revenue doubled last quarter while it spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure, and it has since borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt. Ukrainian officials accused it of throttling Starlink terminals used on military missions, drawing a senators' probe, and Ukraine now plans an independent satellite system.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Spending on AI turned Meta's quarterly free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion, and it now plans a $95 billion stock sale, its largest ever, to fund AI data centres; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eye up to $5 billion of it. Days earlier it lost a New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica and was told to pay $25 billion.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: The Yemen war reached Aramco's own sites. After the Saudi-led coalition hit a Houthi site, a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran. Days later the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, and a Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field pushed Brent to $110.63.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla unveiled its 2026 Roadster at a price of at least $200,000, then reported net profit down 43% to $787 million as margins shrank. The same week, Tesla and SpaceX were reported to be exploring a merger that would combine companies holding 30,000 BTC. The share kept rising through the weak results, alongside the merger talk.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: The only item in the fortnight's feed was MIT Technology Review's visit to Samsung's new semiconductor hub, and it reports no result, order or ruling that would account for the share price.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan called a strike in Taoyuan after a dispute over bonuses escalated. Nothing reported in the window ties the strike, or any other event at the company, to the share price.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: The fortnight's one report on the company's own business was Belgium declining to cover Mounjaro, and that does not account for the share's rise.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Nigeria's central bank, the CBN, granted JPMorgan approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank, a first licensing step for a lender in Lagos since 1961. When Bank of America fell on a $1.2B money-laundering penalty, JPMorgan held steady. Neither accounts for the share's slide.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK hynix cancelled a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion, pulling the storage unit's offering while its own record US listing sat underwater. Nothing else in the input concerns the company's own business, and none of it accounts for the earlier slide.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: China's share of ASML's sales jumped from 14% to 23%, with its equipment sales there up 109% despite a US export curb push. Customers are already asking for lithography tools for 2029 and 2030. Neither story accounts for the share price's move.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The fall came alongside a wider crypto sell-off in which nearly $1 billion in bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. On the network itself, developers set Oct. 21 for the Alpenglow upgrade targeting 150-millisecond finality, and the Firedancer team began charging 1 SOL per bug report after AI-generated submissions swamped triage.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The slide came with a market-wide washout: nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP fell, and traders then fled altcoins for bitcoin. A bug fix on the XRP Ledger slipped to November after validator support dipped, and Ripple's final approval for a national trust bank did not lift the token.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The only Hyperliquid story in the feed was Bloomberg Business on Jeff Yan's plan to bring the entire financial industry onto the network. It describes an ambition, not an event, and nothing in it accounts for the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: The slide into mid-October came with a market-wide washout: nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP fell. The rebound has come in sharp single-day jumps, 11% as AI earnings revived tech and 8% as bitcoin neared $81,000 ahead of the Fed decision.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: No Bank of England decision fell in the fortnight. The argument was over whether to move at all: officials divided over the inflation risk facing the UK, and Greene said those risks were bigger than thought, as gas drove £161 of a £180 rise in UK bills.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The case for tightening further built through October. Ueda said the Bank of Japan can't tolerate underlying inflation running further over 2%, the IMF said it may need to tighten faster if inflation beats forecast, and the finance minister said Japan is shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China has been acting through levers other than this rate. It plans a bond-market liquidity backstop that lends to funds, not just banks, and is piloting onshore yuan trade for foreign banks. It also bought 23 tonnes of gold in September.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia kept its key rate on hold on Friday and named high inflation expectations as a point of concern. It credited rising export revenues for the ruble's strength, and the ruble's climb slowed after the decision. The bank also kept buying yuan through the month.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Bangkok hosted the IMF and World Bank meetings. There Georgieva warned of strained public finances and Warsh called AI a shock to the economy, but none of it concerned Thailand's market. The region also faced a prolonged Hormuz closure and an energy crisis that has Southeast Asians scaling back weddings. Nothing here ties either to the index.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles and drones reached Saudi oil infrastructure: an Aramco building in Dhahran, the route out through Yanbu, the East-West pipeline. The Houthis also told Aramco shareholders to sell, and Riyadh pushed its investor summit to 2027. The rebound came as Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The UAE's non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter. Since then France has secured 200,000 tonnes of extra diesel a month from the UAE and Bahrain, and the UAE and Greece have announced $14.3bn in deals. None of it accounts for the swings in Dubai's property and bank shares.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Inflation hit 7.2% in September against a 2-4% target, and the central bank answered with a jumbo half-point hike, raising borrowing costs for the domestic firms and households this market lives on. Oil above $110 after a Houthi drone strike near the Saudi Shaybah field fed the price pressure, as 22.6% of Filipino families went hungry.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: New Mexico won a $25 billion judgment against Meta over Cambridge Analytica-era deception, and days later the quarter showed AI spending had pushed free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion. Meta answered with new nonvoting shares and a $95bn stock sale, its largest ever, to fund AI data centres, diluting existing holders.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, the money going into AI data centres. Earlier it walked away from Nscale's planned AI site at Loughton, where grid power may not arrive until the 2030s.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: In Bangkok, Fed Chair Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and gave no guidance on the October meeting. By the week of the decision the talk was of a pause with a nod to December, and TD Securities looked for 3 dissents against Wednesday's hold.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The fortnight's news about Tencent's own business was product news: free search calls for developers building AI agents, and the WorkBuddy agent added to WeCom's contact list. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The week's high came as Amazon pledged €16 Billion in Germany for data centers and Prime, a bet on capacity for the AI trade. Days earlier it launched AI devices that listen to and remember conversations. Most other Amazon headlines in the window concern the rainforest, not the company.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX said it spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure last quarter, putting the profit from a doubling of revenue into AI rather than launches. Kyiv accused it of throttling Ukraine's Starlink, with drone links dropping at 110 km/h, and a NASA adviser said Artemis IV would need 22 Starship refuelling flights.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The war with the Houthis reached the company itself: a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and days later the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, as Iran's state agency Mehr reported. Meanwhile Saudi Arabia's output sank to a record 6.24 million barrels daily.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia's own news in the period came mostly from China: Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months as Nvidia's share of that market fell, and iFlytek said it trained Spark X2.6 without Nvidia. Nvidia also joined AMD and Broadcom in eyeing up to $5 billion of Meta stock. None of this was reported as the cause of the share's fall.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The fighting moved away from Sanaa. Houthi missiles killed at least 18 recruits at a training camp in Shabwa, hit the presidential palace in Aden, and reached Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Riyadh airport. Iran backed a 'political process', and nothing reported showed a ground push on the capital.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman, the two states whose coasts form the Strait of Hormuz, reach an agreement on the strait before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through that channel.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.recent: Tehran moved to run the strait alone rather than share it. Araghchi set out Iran's rules for managing Hormuz after the war, and Iran threatened Sinokor's tankers with legal action from 1 November for crossing violations. Khamenei backed Tehran's war conditions, and the mediation with Washington runs through Qatar, not Oman.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Fighting widened instead of pausing: the Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, said Saudi strikes killed 16 people, and declared Riyadh's airport a military target. Talks in Tehran on Monday, where Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president, ended in an agreement to keep talking, not a truce.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The war reached Saudi soil: Houthi missiles targeted the East-West pipeline, a drone attack at Dammam airport killed two, and the Houthis declared Riyadh's airport a military target. Riyadh answered with allies. Egypt's parliament voted to defend it, Pakistan ratified the Makkah defence pact, and its defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: The odds firmed as Washington pressed for a Ukraine deal: Witkoff headed to Russia as Zelenskyy praised the US talks, and Trump urged Ukraine to settle. Since then Putin's aide has said Washington cannot force Kyiv to comply, and Lavrov expects the war to escalate. None of it involved Xi, the contract's third name.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 2. Its price is what traders will stake on a deal that would reopen the Gulf's main oil export route.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Tehran hardened its terms. Khamenei endorsed security chief Mohsen Rezaei's conditions for peace talks. Iran also threatened Sinokor's tankers with legal action from 1 November for breaching the transit rules it imposes on Hormuz, treating the strait as its own regulated waterway while Doha still mediates with Washington.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the war pausing this year.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.recent: Talks in Oslo and Witkoff's meeting with Putin put a settlement back on the table, and Trump paused new Russia sanctions while pressing Kyiv to make a deal. The Kremlin has since confirmed Abu Dhabi talks for November but says Putin wants a final settlement, not a short truce, and Lavrov says the war will continue and likely escalate.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google softened its Gmail ad-targeting promise on 16 October, and four days later its only UK cloud region failed at 06:08 GMT. Those were the company's own stories in the fortnight, and nothing here ties either of them to the fall in its share price.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The bet sank as the war widened: the Houthis hit Aden and Saudi oil sites, then fired 10 ballistic missiles at the East-West pipeline and declared Riyadh's airport a military target. It recovered part of the way when Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran and Khamenei backed peace conditions.

wiki-france.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on France each day. Its peaks mark the days events in the country reached people well beyond its borders.
wiki-france.recent: France's school protests became a wider political crisis: police arrested nearly 2,400 people in one night, Macron rejected his interior minister's resignation, and Paris got an 11pm curfew. Trump and Netanyahu blamed migrants and Islam for the riots, which Macron rebuked, as the 10-year bond yield reached 4.96%, its highest since 2002.

wiki-starlink.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Starlink, SpaceX's network of thousands of low-orbit satellites selling broadband to homes, ships, aircraft and armies, Ukraine's front-line drone units among them.
wiki-starlink.recent: SpaceX capped the speed at which Ukraine's Starlink terminals hold a link, and drones lost contact at 110 km/h, disrupting Kyiv's attacks. Trump said Musk had restored access; Ukrainian sources saw no change, and Kyiv now plans its own satellites. Lithuania foiled an arson attack on a Starlink site, the third NATO state to see one.

stocks:3690.HK.standing: China's largest platform for food delivery and local services, from restaurant orders to hotel bookings, listed in Hong Kong. Its margins swing on subsidy wars with rivals and on Beijing's rules for delivery couriers.
stocks:3690.HK.recent: In Brazil, Keeta found over half of the Rio chain outlets it targeted already tied to iFood by exclusive deals, and it is working around them. That arrived after this month's swings in the share, and nothing in the input explains them.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Diplomacy and strike planning ran side by side: Khamenei backed the conditions for peace talks set by security chief Mohsen Rezaei, and Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, while Trump said the US may strike Iran as soon as Sunday. None of it addressed the uranium stockpile itself.

stocks:300750.SZ.standing: Contemporary Amperex Technology, the Ningde company listed in Shenzhen and the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries. Carmakers from Tesla to BYD's rivals buy its cells, so its share tracks the EV and grid-storage build-out.
stocks:300750.SZ.recent: Contemporary Amperex reported a quarterly profit of 21.2 billion yuan, and its shares still fell 15%. The drop came as China's tech stocks were repriced, with investors weighing earnings against valuations, so a strong quarter did not protect the stock.

stocks:BARC.L.standing: Britain's second-largest bank by assets, combining a UK high-street bank and the Barclaycard business with one of the few European investment banks still competing on Wall Street. Its share price follows both UK rates and trading revenue.
stocks:BARC.L.recent: Barclays said it would cut 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its staff, as AI starts creating efficiency, while paying shareholders £500 million. A day later it vowed to redeploy staff to offset the pain of the cuts.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats control the US Senate after the 2026 midterm elections. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet officers, so whoever holds it decides who a president can appoint.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only American election story in the fortnight was Washington charging former FBI officials over their 2023 testimony, landing 11 days before the midterms. Nothing in it, or in the rest of the input, accounts for what traders were paying on the Senate.

stocks:7782.T.standing: The shares of Sincere Co., a Japanese company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and priced in yen. The quote tracks what investors pay for one share of the company's own business.

stocks:CMCSA.standing: America's largest cable operator, selling Xfinity broadband, TV and mobile, and the owner of NBCUniversal's studios, Peacock and theme parks. Its broadband subscriber count is the figure its shareholders watch most closely.
stocks:CMCSA.recent: Comcast reported losing 144,000 US broadband customers last quarter. It blamed rivals' cheap prices, which it called "irrational", rather than its own service.

poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Banco de México cuts its overnight rate by a quarter point after November. That rate sets borrowing costs across Mexico and the yield gap that draws foreign money into the peso.
